root.name: Italian Game: Evans Gambit Accepted
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4

overview: White has given the b-pawn for time and plays 5.c3 and 6.d4 to build a strong pawn centre while Black's bishop retreats (usually to a5 or e7, or c5 after 5...Ba5 6.d4 d6). White gets a lead in development and attacking chances against f7, while Black can return the pawn at the right moment to get out safely. Both sides need to know the forcing theory.

white_ideas.idea: Build a big centre with c3 and d4, hitting the bishop and opening lines.
Use the lead in development and Bc4 against f7 for a kingside attack.

black_ideas.idea: Retreat the bishop to a5/e7 and return the pawn with ...d6 and ...Bb6 or ...d5.
Neutralise the centre with ...Nf6, ...O-O and a timely ...d5 (Lasker or Pierce defence).

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d4 and e4 against Black's e5, d6 centre; open lines after exchanges.

character.notes: Concrete, forcing lines; both sides can lose fast if they miss a tactic.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the b-pawn; many lines give it back for safety.

soundness.notes: Sound; played by strong players, compensation is sufficient.

structure.notes: Central pawns come off early, open lines for the pieces.

approach.notes: A respectable gambit, standard and played by top players now and then.

level.notes: Needs forcing theory; still approachable, so intermediate.

character.reason: Forcing gambit lines where both sides take risks.

gambit.reason: White gives the b-pawn for development, anchor case.

soundness.reason: Anchor case: playable and not refuted.

structure.reason: Open lines early with the d4 break.

approach.reason: Respectable gambit used by strong players now and then.

level.reason: Forcing theory but a familiar attacking plan.

plans.reason: Pawn sacrificed for development and a big centre.
